What an event planner actually takes on

An event planner builds and runs the plan behind an event. In practice that means turning a brief into a concept, finding and shortlisting a venue, sourcing suppliers and collecting quotes, negotiating and managing contracts, tracking the budget, building the run sheet, and managing the event itself from bump in to bump out.

You will see the same work sold under different labels. A sole practitioner, a small studio and an event planning company with a team of six can all be quoting the same scope, so read the inclusion list rather than the business name. The visible part of the job is the styling. The valuable part is the coordination. A working event planner already knows which caterers will service a dry hire venue in your area, what a realistic bump in window looks like for your room, and which questions to put to a venue before you sign. That knowledge is what you are actually buying.

How much of that list your planner takes is a separate decision from who you hire. Australian planners package their work at three levels, and the level you choose moves the price more than anything else does.

Which kind of event planner do you need?

The job titles are not interchangeable, and asking for the wrong one is the most common reason a quote comes back looking strange. A planner builds the plan. A coordinator runs a plan that already exists. Party planners work to shorter lead times than wedding planners and usually bring a different supplier network with them.

Planner or coordinator?

If you have not booked anything yet, you want a planner. If the plan is largely built and you want someone to run the day, you want a coordinator. The comparison guide sets out where the line actually falls.

Planner vs coordinator

No. 01

Wedding Planners

Weddings have their own vocabulary, their own supplier network and a nine to fourteen month lead time. A wedding planner has run the day before, not just events in general.

No. 02

Party Planners

Birthdays, milestones, engagements and kids parties. Shorter lead times, smaller budgets, and usually the entertainment and hire relationships already in hand.

No. 03

Wedding Coordinators

They take a plan you have already built, confirm every supplier and run the wedding day itself so nobody is ringing the couple about the chairs.

No. 04

Event Coordinators

Coordination for everything that is not a wedding. Logistics, supplier confirmation, run sheets and on-site management for parties, functions and corporate events.

No. 05

Venue Sourcing

A standalone service. A planner shortlists venues against your brief, checks availability and negotiates, without taking on the rest of the plan.

No. 06

Proposal Planning

A short, high stakes event that has to stay secret. Different skill again, and worth going to a specialist for.

Near you

How to find an event planner near you

Almost nobody searching for an event planner near me actually needs one within walking distance. What matters is whether the planner services your area and knows the venues in it.

Event planners work to a service area rather than a shopfront. Most Australian planners cover a whole metropolitan area and a band of country around it, and will travel further for a fee. So searching for event planners near me is really a question about coverage, not distance, and the practical question is not how close a planner is to your house. It is whether they have worked in your area before and what they charge to get there.

Two things are worth checking before you shortlist. The first is whether they have worked at your venue, or at least at venues of that type, because a planner who has done a bump in at your site already knows its restrictions. The second is the travel arrangement, which for regional events can be a meaningful line in the quote and occasionally includes accommodation.

Coverage is deepest in the capital city markets. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth and the Gold Coast all have enough working planners that you can compare several against the same brief. Outside those markets you will usually be talking to planners who travel to you.

Cost

What event planners charge in Australia

Published Australian figures vary widely because they measure different things. Here is what the two most-cited sources actually say.

Australian planner pricing as published by two named sources. These are third-party figures, not a quote for your event.
Pricing modelWhat the published sources saySource
Flat fee, full service$5,000 to $6,000 for complete support covering supplier selection, budgeting, styling and logisticsEasy Weddings, guide updated February 2026
Flat fee, non-wedding eventsFrom around $5,000 for a straightforward event, covering planning fees only and not the event budget itselfFAME Events, September 2024
Percentage of budget10 to 15 per cent of the total event budget, used instead of a flat feeAirtasker Australia cost guide, updated February 2025
Percentage of budget, alternate15 to 20 per cent of budget, described as the less common approachFAME Events, September 2024
Day-of coordinationRoughly $1,500 to $2,000 (Easy Weddings) or $1,000 to $5,000 (Airtasker)Both sources
Hourly consulting$75 to $100 per hour (Easy Weddings) or $70 to $120 per hour (Airtasker)Both sources

Scroll the table sideways to see every column.

Those ranges disagree by thousands of dollars, and the reason is scope rather than error. Our planner cost guide reconciles them and explains which model suits which kind of event.

Before you sign

What to ask before you engage an event planner

Which level am I actually buying?

Get the planner to say, in writing, whether the fee covers full planning, partial planning or coordination only, and what happens to the fee if the scope changes in month four.

How many events do you take at once?

A planner running eight weddings in the same month is a different proposition from one running two. Neither is wrong. You just want to know which you are hiring.

Who is actually at my event?

Some planners run the day personally. Others send a coordinator from their team. Ask which, and ask to meet the person who will be on site.

What is not included?

The exclusions matter more than the inclusions. Common ones are travel outside a set radius, styling hire, extra site visits and additional meetings past a set number.

How do you handle a supplier who fails?

Every experienced planner has a story about a supplier who did not turn up. The answer tells you how they think under pressure and whether they have a backup network.

What does your contract say about cancellation?

Read the deposit, payment schedule and cancellation terms before you sign. This is the part people skip and then regret.

Straight answers

Event planner questions

What is the difference between an event planner and an event coordinator?

An event planner builds the plan from the start: concept, venue, suppliers, budget and timeline. An event coordinator takes a plan that already exists, confirms it and runs it. Many planners offer both, priced as separate packages. If you have booked nothing yet you want a planner. If the plan is largely done you want a coordinator.

How much does an event planner cost in Australia?

Published Australian ranges differ. Easy Weddings, updated February 2026, puts full-service planning at $5,000 to $6,000 and hourly consulting at $75 to $100. Airtasker's Australian guide gives a $1,000 to $20,000 spread with a median around $8,000 and notes a common 10 to 15 per cent of budget model. Australian agency FAME Events says planning for a straightforward event typically starts around $5,000. The right figure for you depends on scope, guest count and how many suppliers need managing.

Do I need an event planner for a small event?

Often not for the whole plan, but frequently for the day. Under about 60 guests, most people can hold the plan themselves. What they cannot do is host and run it at the same time. On-the-day coordination is usually the better value option at that size.

Can an event planner work with suppliers I have already booked?

Yes. Partial planning and coordination are both built around suppliers you have chosen yourself. Tell the planner what is already booked at the enquiry stage, because it changes both the scope and the quote.

Does Plan Your Event plan events?

No. Plan Your Event is a discovery and enquiry service. We pass your enquiry to independent event planners and coordinators who cover your area, and you engage and pay your planner directly.
